title: Rapid Recon: Model Substitutability & Fallback Economics for Regulated Verticals
creator: Nikhil Rao
description:
Summary:
Conduct a focused market reconnaissance to quantify how substitutable open and hosted models are for two regulated verticals (healthcare and legal) when used in short-context Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) scenarios. Objective is to produce a prioritized list of model variants that can be used as fallback candidates for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments, with estimated latency/cost delta and a qualitative risk profile for compliance and model behavior drift.

Scope:
- Surface models and quantized variants that perform acceptably on short-context RAG (<= 1k tokens) for PHI/PII-rich prompts and legal contract extraction tasks.
- Measure substitution cost in three dimensions: latency SLO impact, per-token unit cost, and quality degradation (task-level accuracy/precision for extraction).
- Identify operational constraints (e.g., quantization compatibility, KV cache behavior, sequence length limits) and enterprise friction (license, provenance, KMS/HSM compatibility).
- Deliver guidance for automatic fallback routing rules in Console (e.g., prefer quantized local model when latency > Xms, or fall back to hosted variant with stricter filtering).

Approach / Methodology:
1) Curate a short roster of candidate models across providers and open checkpoints: 3 hosted (provider-A small/medium/large), 4 open (two 7B quantized builds, one 13B int8, one 70B float16 trimmed).
2) Develop a 120-sample short-context prompt set derived from real customer anonymized transcripts (10 customers across healthcare/legal, sanitized) focusing on extraction and redaction tasks.
3) Run microbench harness (benchmarks/redwood-rag-mini) in three infra modes: hosted API, Dedicated-quantized, Private-VPC on a single node. Collect latency, CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, and task accuracy.
4) Annotate failure modes (hallucination, PII leakage, truncated context) and map to remediation levers (prompt engineering, filtering, additional retrieval heuristics).

Acceptance criteria:
- Deliver a ranked fallback catalog (CSV) with: model_key, deployment_mode, median p95 latency delta vs control, cost per 1k tokens estimate, accuracy delta on extraction tasks, known regulatory friction notes.
- Provide a concise Console policy draft (2-3 rules) for automated fallback that can be implemented by runtime in runtime-1.20.
- Present findings to SRE, Security, and SalesOps with an annotated dashboard (Grafana link) and an action backlog of follow-ups.

Deliverables:
- Ranked fallback catalog CSV (artifact stored in Drive).
- Benchmark harness PR (github.com/redwood-inference/rag-mini PR #148).
- Grafana dashboard link with latency/cost/quality panels.
- Confluence findings doc with recommended Console routing rules and a risk matrix.

Risks & Trade-offs:
- Sampling bias: short-context probe may not generalize to long-form customer usage — will document limitations and propose follow-on long-context study.
- Cost vs quality: some quantized builds show acceptable latency but ~5-8% extraction drop — need policy decision on acceptable quality floor for regulated PII tasks.
- Licensing/provenance: some open checkpoints have unclear provenance; flag as "procurement-risk-high" and require legal review before Private deployment.
